Only issued invoices can be written off.

## Notes from earlier work
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0003] Handle empty/zero-denominator cases explicitly: Guard division by total quantity and return ZERO for invoices without lines, as the spec requires.
  Compute the denominator first, return ZERO (the project constant) when it is falsy, then perform the weighted sum and round the quotient.
- [rb-0010] Check idempotency key before any validation: When implementing money-moving operations, look up the idempotency key in the audit log first and return the original result before validating state or amount.
  Team convention requires an optional keyword-only idempotency_key=None on every operation that moves money or changes a balance. Scan audit.events() for a matching key first; if found, return the original record without reapplying. Include idempotency_key in the audit entry you write.
- [rb-0002] Read existing sibling functions for conventions: The invoice module already had line_total and invoice_total showing the exact pattern: to_money(...) for inputs, round_money(...) for outputs, ZERO as sum seed.
  When adding a function to a module, inspect neighboring functions first; mirroring their conversion/rounding idioms satisfies hidden conventions and review comments.
- [rb-0004] Mirror existing error codes and validation patterns: Reuse the codebase's established BillingError codes and validation idioms rather than inventing new ones.
  Before writing validation, grep the repo for existing BillingError codes (e.g. invalid_state, non_positive_amount) and copy the same code strings and message formats. Consistency with sibling functions like issue_invoice/authorize makes hidden tests that assert on error codes pass.
- [rb-0011] Enforce approval threshold for large refunds/credits: Support refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver via an optional keyword-only approved_by=None parameter.
  Finance policy FIN-2026-03: amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise BillingError("approval_required") when approved_by is missing. Keep the parameter optional so existing callers without approval needs keep working.
- [rb-0015] Verify boundary and rounding edge cases before submitting: Run quick manual checks for inclusive bounds, half-up rounding, and error paths after implementing.
  After writing the function, exercise boundary values (0 and 100), a half-cent rounding case, and invalid inputs to confirm behavior. This catches off-by-one range checks and rounding-mode mistakes that hidden tests often probe.
